The Fable of Clawd

A 2 minute 4K film made entirely in Blender, from one prompt on Fable 5.2. It took about 4.5 hours.

Claude built every asset in Blender by writing Python:
- 5 characters and props: Clawd, his friend Pip, a toy truck, a 3D-printed tulip and a gift box
- 7 full sets: a study, a staircase, a street, a workshop, an airport, a night sky and a house
- every camera move and every frame of animation across 52 shots

That came to 12,500 lines of code. It started 7 copies of itself to build the sets at the same time.

Then it rented 89 GPUs through RunPod to render 3,220 frames as fast as possible, 36 of them running at once. Total cost: a little over $20.

My biggest takeaway is my Claude Code knows it has access to cloud compute, so it's much more ambitious.

I tried a similar prompt on my other computer that doesn't have the runpod skill setup and it wasn't nearly as high quality

Full details linked below.

text: The traffic from agent swarms doing research is going to be quite large, they are relentless. I had Fable 5.2 reconstruct WH Auden's 1941 poetry class. It found an obscure, relevant book on the Internet Archive, which it read a line at a time by doing repeated full text searches.

But we also don't want to stop agents from doing relevant academic research (or even commercial research, since it might mention your product) with too many gates and barriers.

In any case, I donated to the Internet Archive for my use of the commons, but better solutions needed.

The end result of the reconstruction is very impressive, however. It made a version of the lost class, called the “hardest in the humanities," that is remarkably accessible and based on scattered textual evidence from Auden's writing & surviving notes. https://auden-english-135.netlify.app/#/tempest/song/0

You can find out tonight which half of your job AI already does.

Anthropic's CEO just named the first to go: entry-level law, finance and consulting. 6,500 people saved the clip. Almost none of them will check their own job.

Here's the prompt that does it in 10 minutes and tells you what's still yours.

What Dario Amodei said, talking with JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon: "AI can do entry-level law work. It can do entry-level finance. It can do entry-level consulting." His forecast hasn't moved since last year: half of entry-level white-collar jobs disrupted in 1 to 5 years. His advice to a kid finishing high school: learn to use AI.

Here's what the clip skips. AI takes tasks first. Your job is 20 to 40 tasks, and some of them it already does faster than you. People who know exactly which ones get to decide what to do with the free hours. Everyone else finds out from their manager.

Prompt 1: Job audit
"I work as [role] at [type of company]. Here is a normal week, with rough hours: [paste your calendar or list your tasks]. For each task, give me a table: the task, hours per week, can current AI do it (yes now / yes with my review / not yet), what exactly AI would do and what stays with me, and the tool I'd use. Be specific. Don't invent percentages you can't back up, and don't tell me my job is safe or doomed. Then give me: total hours AI could take off my week, the 3 tasks that are most mine and why, and 2 skills that make those tasks worth more."

Prompt 2: 30-day plan
"Using the audit above, give me a 30-day plan. Week 1: hand AI the 2 easiest tasks and write me the exact prompts for them. Week 2: set up a review step so I catch its mistakes in under 10 minutes. Weeks 3 and 4: put the freed hours into the 2 skills, one concrete practice task per week. End with the one result I should show my manager on day 30."

Run it on your own week tonight. If AI takes 10 hours off it, that's a quarter of your week back. Decide what to do with it before someone else does.
